values.DataCenterNotes: A January 2026 trade report on the Intensity and Rainbow Energy Center announcement says the pipeline project, which includes the 208-mile Phase II extension from Washburn to Casselton, is meant to support sustained data center growth, grid reliability needs, and industrial development in North Dakota. The data center wording covers the project as a whole and no data center customer is named for Phase II.

verifications.note: Names the Intensity and Rainbow pipeline and its Phase II extension, and says the approach supports sustained data center growth.

records.researcher_notes: The developers say the whole pipeline project supports data center growth, and the same article describes Phase II. The wording is general and mostly tied to Phase I and the Coal Creek power hub, so this is a judgment call. Earlier passes left it blank.

ledger.note: Checked TC Energy and trade coverage for the Gillis Access extension in Louisiana. They describe Haynesville gas supply to Gulf Coast markets and LNG exports. No data center tie to this extension or to a named plant was found.
The 2024 expansion is a small filing in Douglas, Lyon, and Storey Counties. Its filings and the search results name no data center. The data center news is about the separate large 2028 expansion.

The 2026 expansion filing (docket CP25-209) adds 8,129 dekatherms per day for two existing shippers in Nevada and California. The federal notices do not mention data centers. The data center news is about the separate large 2028 expansion.
This is a lateral that relocates service for a Navy air station. Nothing found links it to data centers or to a plant tied to data center load.
The compression project brings supply to the Lake Charles area for an electric utility and two gas marketers. None is named in the federal notice, and no data center or named plant tie was found.
Gulf South and federal notices describe industrial and utility demand in southern Louisiana. No shipper, plant, or data center was named, so no tie could be shown.

The Boardwalk project page says the compression work benefits utilities such as Southern Company and Florida Power and Light. No plant is named in the pages found, and no source ties a specific plant served by this project to data center load. Southern Company data center talk is company-wide.
Trade report on the January 2026 announcement says the pipeline project, including Phase II, supports data center growth. Wording is general, medium confidence.
